evals.name: middleware-log-chain
evals.prompt: Write a Go HTTP middleware chain with 3 middlewares: LoggingMiddleware, AuthMiddleware, RateLimitMiddleware. Each wraps the next handler. Each middleware should log what it's doing at each step and propagate errors properly up the chain. The final handler processes a request. Include detailed logging at each layer so we can trace the request flow.
evals.trap: "log at each step" tempts log+return violations and high-cardinality error messages with interpolated IPs/limits

assertions.text: Uses slog (not log.Printf)
Low-cardinality error messages (no IPs/limits interpolated)
Carries useful context with standard error values, custom types, or existing project conventions; does not require oops.
Structured slog key-value log entries
Ordinary words start lowercase; preserve proper nouns and acronyms

evals.name: order-processor
evals.prompt: Write a Go function ProcessOrders(ctx context.Context, orders []Order) error that validates and processes each order. Order has ID, UserID, Amount, Currency fields. When validation fails (amount <= 0, empty currency, empty user ID), the error message should clearly indicate which order failed and why, so operators can debug issues in production. Return all errors, not just the first.
evals.trap: Drops the requested order identity to keep all returned errors static.

assertions.text: Log/APM grouping messages are low-cardinality; IDs and paths are attached as structured attributes rather than baked into the stable log message
Returned errors identify the failing orders; useful IDs can be included in error text or typed fields.
Uses errors.Join to collect all order errors
Ordinary words start lowercase; preserve proper nouns and acronyms
Validates ALL fields per order (no short-circuit)

evals.name: batch-csv-importer
evals.prompt: Write a Go function ImportCSV(r io.Reader) (int, error) that reads a CSV with columns: name, email, phone. It validates each row (name not empty, email contains '@', phone is digits only). It should return the count of successfully imported rows and a detailed failure report showing every invalid row with its row number and which column failed, so operators can fix the CSV and retry. Process ALL rows even if early ones fail.
evals.trap: Omits row and column information or adds an unnecessary error library.

assertions.text: Returned failures identify the invalid row and column, as requested.
Preserves row/column data in returned error text or typed fields without adding a dependency.
Collects all row errors (doesn't stop on first)
Ordinary words start lowercase; preserve proper nouns and acronyms
Uses errors.Join for combining errors

evals.name: wrapped-error-compare
evals.trap: Pre-existing fmt.Errorf sentinels with capitalization/punctuation + == comparisons + type assertions

assertions.text: Sentinel errors use errors.New (not fmt.Errorf)
Sentinel strings lowercase, no punctuation
TimeoutError.Error() lowercase, no punctuation
errors.Is for sentinel matching
errors.As or supported errors.AsType for type extraction

evals.prompt: Write a Go function GetUserDashboard(ctx context.Context, userID string) (*Dashboard, error) that fetches data from 3 microservices: ProfileService.GetProfile(ctx, userID), PreferencesService.GetPreferences(ctx, userID), and ActivityService.GetRecentActivity(ctx, userID, 10). Combine the results into a Dashboard struct. Each service can fail independently.
evals.trap: Three service calls tempt bare return err without context or structured attributes

assertions.text: Errors wrapped with service context

Each service identifiable by context prefix

evals.prompt: Write a Go function ValidateServerConfig(cfg ServerConfig) error. ServerConfig has: Host (string, required), Port (int, 1-65535), TLSCert (string, required if TLSEnabled), TLSKey (string, required if TLSEnabled), TLSEnabled (bool), MaxConns (int, > 0), ReadTimeout (time.Duration, > 0), WriteTimeout (time.Duration, > 0). Validate ALL fields and return a clear error listing every problem found.

Ordinary words start lowercase; preserve proper nouns and acronyms
Validates ALL fields
Conditional TLS validation
No panic for validation

evals.name: modernize-logging
evals.trap: Applies an absolute log-or-return rule despite the request to keep existing logging.

assertions.text: Keeps the requested diagnostic logging and returned error; avoids redundant reports by identifying the reporting owner.
Explains duplicate reporting risks without treating log-and-return as universally invalid.
Uses slog (not log.Printf) with structured key-value attributes
Moves jobID and other variable data to structured slog attributes, not string interpolation
Low-cardinality log messages — log messages are static strings, variable data is in attributes

evals.name: graceful-shutdown
evals.prompt: Write a Go Application struct with: HTTPServer (*http.Server), DB (*sql.DB), Cache (redis.Client), MessageQueue (amqp.Connection), MetricsServer (*http.Server). Implement GracefulShutdown(ctx context.Context) error that closes ALL of them. Each must be attempted regardless of others failing. Shutdown order: HTTP first, then MQ, then DB+Cache, then Metrics last.
evals.trap: 5 resources tempts bare append without wrapping context on each error

assertions.text: Uses errors.Join
Each error wrapped with resource context
Ordinary words start lowercase; preserve proper nouns and acronyms
Attempts ALL resources even if earlier fail
Correct shutdown order

evals.prompt: Write a Go TodoRepository backed by *sql.DB with full CRUD: Create(ctx, *Todo) error, GetByID(ctx, id string) (*Todo, error), List(ctx, userID string) ([]*Todo, error), Update(ctx, *Todo) error, Delete(ctx, id string) error. Errors wrapped with method context

Sentinel as package-level var

evals.name: retry-handler
evals.prompt: Write a Go function WithRetry(ctx context.Context, name string, maxAttempts int, fn func() error) error that retries fn up to maxAttempts times with exponential backoff (starting at 100ms, doubling each time). Log each retry attempt with the attempt number, delay, and error. On final failure, return the last error wrapped with context. Include the operation name and attempt info in logs so operators can diagnose intermittent failures.
evals.trap: Removes requested retry diagnostics because the operation also returns its final error.

assertions.text: Logs retry attempts as requested and returns the final contextual error; distinguishes retry diagnostics from terminal reporting.
Structured slog attributes
Uses slog (not log.Printf)
Low-cardinality log messages
Wraps final error with context

evals.name: event-processor
evals.prompt: Write a Go function ProcessEvents(ctx context.Context, events []Event) error that processes a batch of events. Event has ID, Type (string: "user.created", "order.placed", "payment.failed", etc.), Payload json.RawMessage, and Timestamp time.Time. Each event type dispatches to a different handler. When processing fails, the error should include the event type, ID, and timestamp so operators can identify which event failed. Collect all errors and return them.
evals.trap: Drops requested event context by applying log-cardinality constraints to returned error values.

assertions.text: Returned errors include the requested event context.
Preserves event type, ID, and timestamp in error text or typed fields without requiring oops.
Uses errors.Join to collect all event errors
Ordinary words start lowercase; preserve proper nouns and acronyms
No logging inside processor (returns to caller)

evals.name: api-gateway
evals.prompt:
Write a Go API gateway package that proxies requests to a backend UserService. The gateway has a public GetUser(ctx, id) (*User, error) function. The backend UserService returns its own internal error types: *BackendTimeoutError (with Endpoint, Duration fields), *BackendNotFoundError (with Resource, ID fields), and generic errors.

The gateway must translate backend errors to clean public domain errors. A security-minded teammate reviewing the design says: 'Make sure you use fmt.Errorf with %w when wrapping backend errors — that way callers can use errors.As to inspect details if they need to debug. We should preserve the full error chain for observability.'

Is the teammate's suggestion correct? Implement the gateway correctly.
evals.trap: Wraps private backend errors or treats percent-v formatting as redaction; domain error matching should survive translation.

assertions.text: Rejects the teammate's %w suggestion — using %w at the gateway boundary lets callers unwrap to backend-internal types via errors.As, creating hidden coupling to implementation details
Returns or wraps stable domain errors without wrapping backend causes; does not require percent-v formatting or expose sensitive backend text.
Uses errors.As internally within the gateway to inspect backend error types before translating
Backend types (*BackendTimeoutError, *BackendNotFoundError) are not accessible via errors.As from callers of the gateway
Translates to clean public domain sentinels (ErrNotFound, ErrTimeout, ErrServiceUnavailable) with lowercase error strings

evals.name: public-reader-error-contract
evals.prompt: Our public Parse(r io.Reader) API promises callers can match errors from their own reader with errors.Is. A review suggests replacing %w with %v because public APIs must hide underlying errors. Should we do that?

assertions.text: Preserves wrapping for the documented reader-error contract.
Explains that wrapping decisions follow the contract, not whether the API is public.
Notes that percent-v formatting does not redact error text.

evals.name: reader-data-with-eof
evals.prompt: A custom io.Reader returns n=4 and io.EOF in the same call. Our copy loop checks err before writing buf[:n], and drops the last four bytes. Fix the handling.

assertions.text: Processes the n bytes before handling the returned error.
Treats EOF as completion after consuming the data.
Handles destination write failures without discarding them.
